trackers.product_line: X-Mode location SDK; in 2021 X-Mode moved its business to Outlogic, a wholly owned subsidiary of Digital Envoy, whose majority owner is Landmark Media Enterprises
data_collected: precise location (latitude and longitude) with a timestamp
the advertising ID (MAID) and installation IDs
trackers.monetization_model: Paid app makers to embed its SDK ("passive revenue" for each device that shares its location, per the FTC), then licensed the raw location data, tied to advertising IDs, and audience segments built from it. Since 2021 the business runs as Outlogic, which licenses location data to ad networks, data resellers, financial institutions and governments (Outlogic's privacy notice).

data_flows.wording: Settled with the US FTC (2024); X-Mode and Outlogic neither admitted nor denied the charges.

consequences.text: In 2024 the US FTC barred X-Mode and its successor Outlogic from selling or sharing sensitive location data, such as visits to medical and reproductive health clinics, places of worship and domestic abuse shelters, and ordered them to delete the location data they had collected unless people consent or it is deidentified. The ban covers places in the US.
consequences.wording: Settled with the US FTC (2024); X-Mode and Outlogic neither admitted nor denied the charges.

consequences.text: The FTC also charged that X-Mode didn't tell people their location would be sold to private government contractors for national security purposes, and that from 2018 to 2020 it collected and sold location data from Android users who had opted out of ad personalization. The order doesn't cover data collected outside the US for federal agencies' national security work.
